decision_reason: Avni is a current, substantial open-source field-service/data platform, but it was created and is stewarded by Samanvay Foundation rather than by a government agency. The official project history identifies nonprofit development/funding, so reported government-program use is not counted as provenance. Public source, AGPL-3.0 scope, 2016 open-source start, and current product/notability evidence are recorded separately. No exact GOSDIR match found; no entry added.

government_provenance.note: The official history says Avni began in 2016 as an open-source community-health platform and is developed by Samanvay Foundation, with development funded by Social Alpha and Project Tech4Dev. This is nonprofit/corporate project stewardship, not government creation, commissioning, funding, or stewardship. Use by government programs is not substituted for provenance.

public_source.note: The official Avni GitHub organization publicly exposes the application source components, including the Android field app, web management app, server APIs, data models, reporting and deployment repositories. Core repositories show current 2026 activity.

eligible_license.note: The official Avni project page states AGPL-3.0, and the canonical server and client repositories identify AGPL-3.0 for first-party application code. This finding applies to Avni's own code, not separately licensed dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: Avni's first-party June 2026 product update identifies it as an open-source field platform used by 70+ organizations and reporting 11M+ beneficiaries/100M+ field visits; the current Samanvay site also describes an Andhra Pradesh government education deployment handed over to the state. These support current product identity, use and notability, but not government provenance.

product_identity: Avni, a mobile-first, offline-capable field-service delivery and data collection platform with Android, web administration, server, reporting and deployment components
agency: No government-originating agency identified; Avni is developed/stewarded by Samanvay Foundation and affiliated Samanvay Technologies. Government programs are users, not the source owner.
geography: India, with implementations across development-sector and government programs
license: AGPL-3.0 for Avni first-party application code; individual third-party components and dependencies retain their own licenses
status_note: The official project history dates Avni's start as an open-source project to mid-2016; this is used as the product's first open-source year, not the intake metadata date. The source is active and the June 2026 product update shows current use at scale. Source-screen DPG registration and government use are not treated as proof of government provenance. No exact GOSDIR duplicate found.

decision_reason: BABEL is demonstrably an AUSL Bologna-created document-management platform with publicly accessible source components and strong historical public-administration use. Hold because the product is split across linked repositories and the exact scope of the declared EUPL-1.2 grant could not be independently verified across those components; the earliest public licensed source year is also unresolved. Catalog data gives a 2019 last release and vendor support through 2025-12-31, with no sufficiently current source-to-product/support proof for 2026.

government_provenance.note: AUSL Bologna's official product page identifies BABEL as its document-management platform developed using the agency's own resources, and says it was extended to other Emilia-Romagna health agencies. This is product creation/stewardship, not merely public-sector use.

public_source.note: The agency-owned public project repository describes BABEL and links to the backend framework and the frontend framework/application repositories that comprise the source. Source is publicly accessible, but the product is split across multiple repositories rather than contained in this index repository alone.

eligible_license.note: A root LICENSE.md is present and Developers Italia declares EUPL-1.2, but the license text/scope could not be independently verified here and the source is spread across separately licensed backend/frontend/application repositories. Do not infer that the metadata declaration necessarily grants every linked component.

primary_evidence.note: The official AUSL page establishes real deployment and describes more than 7,000 staff using BABEL, but that usage statement is from the 2015 page. Developers Italia reports 11 administrations, a 2019 last release and support contracts ending 2025-12-31; no current 2026 evidence establishes ongoing deployment/support or the precise source lineage.

product_identity: BABEL, an integrated document-management and workflow platform for health administrations, combining shared services and vertical modules for digital desk, document files, PEC, protocol, acts, signatures and related workflows
agency: Azienda USL di Bologna (AUSL Bologna), original agency developer/owner; other Emilia-Romagna health agencies participated in later development
geography: Italy (Emilia-Romagna; listed adopters include other Italian public administrations)
license: Unresolved: EUPL-1.2 is declared in the official catalog and a root LICENSE.md exists, but the grant scope across the linked component repositories was not verified
status_note: The official AUSL page was published in 2015; that page date is not used as the open-source year. The source index links separate backend and front-end repositories, so the earliest public licensed code year and full grant scope need repository-by-repository verification. Developers Italia's lastRelease 2019-04-01 and support-contract end 2025-12-31 are metadata, not source-year or current-use proof. No exact GOSDIR duplicate found.

decision_reason: DAE RespondER is a Region Emilia-Romagna 118 emergency-response application with current official evidence of regional service use and substantial operational impact. Hold because the assigned public repository exposes only a small JavaScript/HTML set, and it has not been shown to be the canonical source for the current native mobile app/backend (including DAE RespondER 2.0). The actual root EUPL-1.2 grant/scope and first public licensed source year also remain unverified; the catalog's 2019 last-release field is metadata, not source history.

government_provenance.note: The exact repository is under the public Azienda-USL-di-Bologna account and says DAE RespondER was developed by the regional Sistema 118 and integrated with the Region's 118 operation centres. Apple's official listing names Regione Emilia-Romagna as provider and developer.

public_source.note: The public repository contains JavaScript/HTML application-related files, screenshots and documentation, but the visible file set does not establish that it contains the canonical/current mobile application source or the regional backend. The official service is now described as DAE RespondER 2.0, and lineage to this small repository remains unproven.

eligible_license.note: The publiccode record declares EUPL-1.2 and the repository has a root LICENSE.md, but the actual license text/scope could not be inspected here. The metadata declaration alone does not prove that the visible frontend source or current native/backend code is covered.

primary_evidence.note: The official regional 118 site provides current DAE RespondER 2.0 guidance, including integration with the 118 service. The Region's 2024 report records 23,124 registered first responders and describes the app's impact; this verifies a notable, currently supported public emergency-response product, but not source lineage.

product_identity: DAE RespondER, the regional 118 service and mobile application for mapping automated external defibrillators and alerting nearby trained first responders to suspected cardiac-arrest events
agency: Regione Emilia-Romagna Sistema 118; the assigned repository is hosted by Azienda USL di Bologna

decision_reason: Bahmni Core is a public, mature OpenMRS module used within the larger hospital information system, but Bahmni originated at the nonprofit Jan Swasthya Sahyog hospital with ThoughtWorks, not through government creation, commissioning, funding or stewardship. Ministry of Health deployments are adoption, not provenance. Additionally, the exact component license is inconsistent: the repository root is MPL-2.0 while Bahmni's license page says Bahmni components are AGPL-3.0-and-above. Reject on the documented provenance failure; record the license discrepancy separately. No catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: Bahmni's official history says ThoughtWorks began building it in 2013 and the first implementation was at nonprofit hospital Jan Swasthya Sahyog. Ministries of Health later adopted Bahmni nationally in several countries, but those deployments do not establish government authorship or funding of this product.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains substantial Java OpenMRS modules, build instructions and deployment guidance for Bahmni Core, a first-party component of the broader hospital information system.

eligible_license.note: The direct root LICENSE file is the full Mozilla Public License 2.0, while Bahmni's official license page says new Bahmni components/modifications are AGPL version 3.0 and above. The exact license/scope applicable to this repository's code is unresolved; the DPG AGPL metadata is not treated as controlling.

primary_evidence.note: Bahmni's official implementation page and FAQ document major hospital use and Ministry of Health rollouts, but the retrieved named deployment evidence is historical (including the 2018 Lesotho pilot); current deployment of this exact bahmni-core source was not established. This is not outcome-determinative because government provenance fails.

agency: No government-originating agency identified; Bahmni was developed by ThoughtWorks with nonprofit hospital Jan Swasthya Sahyog and is now stewarded by the Bahmni Coalition
geography: India origin; global hospital deployments, including historical Ministry of Health rollouts in multiple countries
license: Unresolved: bahmni-core root LICENSE is MPL-2.0, whereas Bahmni's official license page says Bahmni components are AGPL-3.0-and-above; exact source-code grant/scope needs reconciliation
status_note: Bahmni's official FAQ dates product development to January 2013, but exact first public licensed source for this specific core repository was not resolved, so no source year is inferred from product inception or DPG metadata. This candidate URL is only the OpenMRS core component; ministry use of the full suite is not provenance for it. No exact GOSDIR duplicate found.

decision_reason: Although GanttProject began as an individual student's open-source application, the project's first-party history explicitly documents a substantial 2005 code contribution from Actimage developers sponsored by the French government agency ADAE, followed by release of GanttProject 2.0. The French Senate identifies ADAE as an interministerial state service under the Prime Minister. This is a specific project-development sponsorship link, not government use alone. The official repository contains the current desktop app under GPL-3.0, and its 3.4 Beta VI release on 2026-09-15 plus official product site establish current distribution and substantial use/notability. No exact GOSDIR match found; no entry added.

government_provenance.note: The first-party project history states that in 2005 Actimage developers sponsored by ADAE contributed substantial code to GanttProject and released 2.0. The French Senate identifies ADAE as an interministerial state service attached to the Prime Minister (https://www.senat.fr/rap/r03-422/r03-42211.html). This is direct government-sponsored development of the product; the earlier individual-student origin and the SILL listing are not used alone as provenance.

public_source.note: The official public repository contains the current Java/Kotlin desktop application, build and distribution files, source submodules and user documentation; README instructions build the application from source.

eligible_license.note: The project README and root LICENSE identify GNU GPL-3.0 for the GanttProject application. This grant covers first-party application code; separately licensed libraries/submodules retain their own notices and terms.

primary_evidence.note: The official releases page records GanttProject 3.4 Beta VI released 2026-09-15 with current Windows/macOS/Linux desktop downloads and feature changes; the official product site reports millions of installations across 200+ countries. This establishes current distribution, user-facing product identity and notability.

product_identity: GanttProject, a cross-platform desktop application for project planning with Gantt/PERT charts, task dependencies, resource/cost planning and export
agency: Agence pour le développement de l'administration électronique (ADAE), French government interministerial service, sponsored Actimage contributions to GanttProject in 2005; original product creator Alexandre Thomas was an individual student
license: GNU GPL-3.0 for first-party GanttProject application code; individual submodules and bundled dependencies may carry separate licenses
status_note: The official timeline dates the first version and SourceForge project registration to 2003; SourceForge's archived files show source tarballs from March 2003, and contemporaneous 2003 release reporting identifies GPL licensing. The 2005 ADAE sponsorship is the government-provenance basis, distinct from French SILL inclusion or public-sector use. Current official release is GanttProject 3.4 Beta VI (2026-09-15). No exact GOSDIR duplicate found.
